practice: Track four delivery metrics together: lead time, deployment frequency, time to restore, change-fail rate
source: Forsgren, Humble, Kim (2018) Accelerate, IT Revolution. https://www.porchlightbooks.com/products/accelerate-nicole-forsgren-phd-9781942788331
company: survey of many firms (State of DevOps data)
claims_to_improve: throughput and stability are measured together rather than traded off
loop_mapping: swe-ledger already records throughput and CI/review/integrity outcomes; add per-run lead time (wall_minutes is null in 258 of 265 rows)
headroom_metric: wall_minutes and ci_failures_before_green are the metric inputs

practice: One trunk-based repository with atomic cross-team changes, plus tooling for static analysis, cleanup and review
source: Potvin, Levenberg (2016) Why Google stores billions of lines of code in a single repository, CACM 59(7). https://research.google/pubs/why-google-stores-billions-of-lines-of-code-in-a-single-repository/
claims_to_improve: code sharing, unified versioning, atomic large changes; costs are tooling and codebase complexity
loop_mapping: this portfolio is moving into one monorepo (oss-monorepo) under research/; the mirror already preserves history
headroom_metric: parallel-run collisions on README.md and projects.json

practice: Every change reviewed before commit, with lightweight tool-supported review
source: Sadowski, Soederberg, Church, Sipko, Bacchelli (2018) Modern code review: a case study at Google, ICSE-SEIP, 181-190. https://doi.org/10.1145/3183519.3183525
claims_to_improve: interviews (12), survey (44) and review logs (9 million reviewed changes) describe why and how review is done
loop_mapping: landing runs merge their own PRs; an independent reviewer pass is the analogue (Claude Code Review / swe-audit)

practice: Treat review as knowledge transfer and awareness, not only defect finding
source: Bacchelli, Bird (2013) Expectations, outcomes, and challenges of modern code review, ICSE, 712-721. https://doi.org/10.1109/ICSE.2013.6606617
claims_to_improve: observation, interviews, survey (165 managers, 873 programmers) and 570 classified comments: reviews find fewer defects than expected but spread knowledge
loop_mapping: knowledge transfer between agent sessions has no counterpart: sessions share no memory except files in the repo
headroom_metric: none: sessions do not retain knowledge

practice: Continuous deployment kept productivity and quality while the team grew 20x and the codebase 50x
source: Savor, Douglas, Gentili, Williams, Beck, Stumm (2016) Continuous deployment at Facebook and OANDA, ICSE-C, 21-30. https://www.eecg.toronto.edu/~stumm/Papers/Savor-ICSE16.pdf
claims_to_improve: deploy frequency can rise without hurting quality; the authors say management support appears necessary
loop_mapping: merge-on-green into main plus Pages deploy on every push is already this loop

practice: Autonomous cross-functional squads grouped in tribes, with chapters and guilds across them
claims_to_improve: team autonomy at 30+ teams; the authors describe it as one example, not a framework
loop_mapping: assumes people, meetings and career paths; agent sessions have none, so only the autonomy-with-claims idea (one project per PR, claim before build) maps

practice: Engineers are on call for the services they run, with defined on-call practice
source: Beyer, Jones, Petoff, Murphy (2016) Site Reliability Engineering, O'Reilly, ch. 11 Being On-Call. https://oreilly.com/library/view/site-reliability-engineering/9781491929117/ch11.html
claims_to_improve: operational ownership by the team that builds the service
loop_mapping: no humans are paged; the analogue is the scheduled run that lands or comments a blocker on its own PR (prompt.md Landing work 6)
headroom_metric: leaked branches / PRs not on main after 24h
